messages:
alex: Heads-up: noticed ~18% tail-latency regression after yesterday's kernel-selector change that prefers flash_attn_v2_tiled for seq > 256. microbench (bs=8, seq=512, model=redwood-7b): p95 48ms -> 57ms. Anyone seen this pattern before?
sasha: ugh. which workload? hosted or dedicated?
alex: hosted infra (prod-like dedicated pool). Happens on A100p32 and older A100s. Not on newer H100 test nodes.
mina: can you paste nvprof/Nsight summary? could be shared-mem/occupancy fallout or L2 thrash from KV prefetching.
alex: here are two short captures (before vs after). focus on SMem util + achieved occupancy:
```
BEFORE (flash_attn_fused):
  avg_sm_eff: 52%  achieved_occupancy: 0.78  L2_bw: 620 GB/s
  kernel: flash_attn_fused  blocks: 1024  smem_per_blk: 48 KB  warps_per_blk: 8
  p95_latency: 48.1 ms

AFTER (flash_attn_v2_tiled):
  avg_sm_eff: 31%  achieved_occupancy: 0.46  L2_bw: 610 GB/s
  kernel: flash_attn_v2_tiled  blocks: 1408  smem_per_blk: 96 KB  warps_per_blk: 4
  p95_latency: 57.0 ms
```
alex: also saw extra memcpy activity tied to kv_cache_prefetch when batch>6 -> seems like tiled kernel increases number of prefetch steps which creates more global writes
sasha: smem_per_blk doubled, warps per block halved -> occupancy collapse. tiled variant probably uses bigger tile for memory parallelism but kills occupancy for our batch/seq mix.
kevin: did selector use only seq length heuristic? or also batch/SM capability?
alex: current selector rule: prefer flash_attn_v2_tiled if seq >= 256 OR model.has_sparse_kv==true. No batching or smem cap check.
mina: that's the issue. For seq=512 bs=8 the tiled kernel allocates ~96KB smem which on 64 SM A100 reduces resident blocks. we should add heuristic based on smem_per_block and warp_count to keep occupancy >= 0.6.
sasha: suggestion: compute estimated_occupancy = min(1.0, max_blocks_per_sm * warps_per_block * 32 / (max_warps_per_sm)) and require >=0.6 in selector. or simpler: if smem_per_blk > 64KB prefer fused.
kevin: also consider pipeline stages. the tiled kernel currently uses pipeline_stages=3 to overlap prefetch + compute + writeback. For small batches that adds scheduling overhead. dropping to 2 stages improved latency in my toy runs.
alex: mina, can you sketch the selector patch? I can push canary if we agree.
mina: proposal snippet for selector logic (pseudo):
```
// compute kernel footprints
smem = kernel.smem_est(seq, model_size)
warps = kernel.warps_per_block
est_occ = est_occupancy(device_props, smem, warps)
if est_occ < 0.6 and batch_size <= 16:
  prefer fused_attn
elif seq >= 1024 and device_mem_bw > threshold:
  prefer tiled_v2
else:
  default to fused_attn
```
mina: also want a quick microbench suite for combinations: bs={1,2,4,8,16}, seq={128,256,512,1024}, kernels={fused, tiled_v2, flash_v1}, device={A100,A100p32,H100}. run ~10 warmups, 50 samples.
kevin: tiny nit: KV cache prefetch path currently does per-request memcpy of full prefix block for tiled kernel. we can change to page-granular prefetch (64KB) and async copy to reduce extra GDR copies. that should reduce global memory writes we observed.
alex: good catch. the memcpy spikes align with prefix copy times in logs. perf-bot: microbench job submitted: job/1772 (bs sweep)
perf-bot: results posted: job/1772 finished. Summary: for bs=8 seq=512 A100p32: fused_attn p95=49.0ms, tiled_v2 p95=56.8ms. But for seq=1536 tiled_v2 wins by ~12%.
sasha: so we need selector that is seq-aware and occupancy-aware. Also add KV prefetch switch to page-granular for tiled variant.
mina: I'll open a small PR with selector changes + unit tests for est_occupancy and a feature-flag to revert if any canary alerts.
alex: plan: 1) rollback canary in prod if regression >10% for p95 until patch lands; 2) land selector + prefetch change behind feature flags; 3) run microbench matrix and gradelog performance tests; 4) schedule canary with gradual traffic shift.
kevin: add a perf regression test that exercises bs=8 seq=512 as a guard so future selector flips don't regress.
mina: noted. I'll add to ci/perf-suite a new case and include Nsight summary assertion on achieved_occupancy > 0.55 for chosen kernel.
sasha: lgtm. thanks team. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — will coordinate rollback if perf-bot flags spikes.
perf-bot: alert: canary-pool p95 jumped by 14% (timestamp 1710723568)
alex: rolling back selector in canary now.
sasha: follow-up item: document heuristics in docs/kernel-selection.md and add a short note about shared memory sizing rules for kernel authors.
mina: allocating that doc now.
kevin: once stable we can consider adding an automated tuner that picks tile size at runtime based on occupancy and L2 utilization. low-priority but nice.
alex: good idea, but let's fix the selector + prefetch first. thanks everyone.
